$comment: Machine-readable protocol constants. This file is the single source of truth for tag values, score bounds and byte lengths. Specifications state the rules; this file states the values. A change here is a protocol version change per SPEC-010.
opReturnTagsComment: Push-only ASCII tags. lengthBytes is the byte length of the tag itself, which determines the direct-push opcode it is encoded with.

RATING2.$comment: SPEC-004 RF-08. Same single-use Rating Right spend, adds a 32-byte commentHash (see commentHash below).

RETRACT.$comment: SPEC-004 RF-06/RF-07. Unilateral rating retraction; payload is the referenced Receipt txid (32 bytes, display order).

scoreRange.$comment: SPEC-004 RF-04. Values outside this range are NOT dropped: the fact is emitted with valid=false. See SPEC-009 RF-W08.

encodedRange.$comment: The encoded form is a single unsigned byte, so a malformed or out-of-range value can still be 0-255.

fieldLengths.$comment: Byte lengths of the fixed-width protocol fields. All are rendered as lowercase hex in facts.

receiptCommitment.$comment: SPEC-003 RF-08 / SPEC-009 §9.2. Optional interaction context in the Receipt's NFT commitment. 4-byte form: 0x10 · category · roleA · roleB. 36-byte form: 0x11 · category · roleA · roleB · contextHash (32 bytes). The empty commitment is the legacy form. Any other length is not a fact (SPEC-009 RF-W73).

preimage.$comment: The interaction contextHash has NO published preimage (SPEC-003 RF-08; decision P6 in audit/lote2/A-DECISIONES.md). This entry records only the byte-length fact of the prefix so a producer does not truncate it: 'REPID-RCTX-V1' is 13 ASCII bytes (0x52455049442d524354582d5631), corrected from an earlier 12-byte claim. No SHA-256 formula is defined over these bytes.

commentHash.$comment: SPEC-004 RF-08/RF-09/RF-10. REPID_RATING2 attaches a 32-byte commentHash to the score. The comment itself is never on-chain; hash fidelity is an off-chain claim. commentHash := SHA256('REPID-CMT-V1' ‖ receiptCategory(32, display order, the Receipt the rating belongs to) ‖ raterPkh(20) ‖ saltLen(1 byte) ‖ salt ‖ comment), saltLen 16..32.

contracts.$comment: Verified with cashc 0.13.2. WARNING: the 'fingerprint' the compiler emits is NOT a conformance anchor. Empirically it does not change when the contract's logic changes: editing `require(tx.outputs.length == 2)` to `== 3` altered the compiled bytecode, the embedded source and the debug bytecode, while the fingerprint stayed identical. It is recorded here for traceability only. Conformance is established by tools/check-artifacts.mjs, which recompiles each source and compares the full artifact (mnemonic bytecode, ABI, embedded source, debug bytecode) against the committed one.

identityVault.$comment: Versioned covenant registry since 0.4.0. `version` names the body carried by the flat fields, which stay the 0.3.0 body; `versions` maps each protocol version to the covenant source, artifact and recorded fingerprint. 0.3.0 is frozen (its burn path has no delay), 0.4.0 adds `require(this.age >= 144)` (SPEC-008 RF-O831, `identityVault.minBurnDelayBlocks`). 0.5.0 changes no covenant, so it records the 0.4.0 body under its own name: an implementation that declares 0.5.0 has canonical bytes to bind against without trial matching (SPEC-009 RF-W56/RF-W76). Built by tools/build-covenant-bytecode.mjs and checked by tools/check-artifacts.mjs.

ratingRight.$comment: RFC-004. RatingRightVault is referenced by ReceiptGenesisValidator through its P2SH32 hash, not by name: CashScript 0.13 cannot import a contract, build a LockingBytecode from raw bytes, or concatenate byte strings.

identityVault.$comment: SPEC-008 RF-O831. burn() requires this.age >= 144 blocks (~24 h). Compiled and VM-verified in task E (conformance/identity-vault-burn-delay.test.mjs, libauth VM at BCH_2026_05): sequences below 144, sequences with the CSV disable flag set, and seconds-unit sequences are rejected; the burn must declare a relative-lock sequence in block units.

outOfScope.$comment: Values that are often mistaken for protocol constants but belong to the application layer. They MUST NOT be added to this file.
outOfScope.DEFAULT_IDENTITY_COLLATERAL: application default (demo server), not a protocol invariant
outOfScope.reputationWeights: interpretation layer, see SPEC-007 in the demo repository
outOfScope.confidenceIndex: interpretation layer, see SPEC-007 in the demo repository
